card.name: Punctuation before a warning instruction
card.fires_on: Commas, periods and colons that end a hazard or warning clause, right before an instruction such as 'should not', 'never', or 'ensure'. Seen in warning labels, caution notes and safety advice.

modes.label: Comma after purpose or risk clause
modes.description: A comma closes a clause about avoiding harm and a prohibition follows.
modes.example: To prevent unintentional overdose<<,>> this product should not be used in pediatric

modes.label: Colon after WARNING or CAUTION
modes.description: A colon after a warning heading leads into a command.
modes.example: Figure 13 CAUTION<<:>> NEVER TOUCH THE GREEN NEEDLE SHIELD

modes.label: Period after a hazard statement
modes.description: A period ends a sentence describing a harm, and the next sentence gives further warnings.
